summary: The window shows an escalating standoff between Iran and Western/Gulf states over the Strait of Hormuz and Iranian oil shipments, culminating on Day 13 with British Royal Marines seizing an oil tanker off Gibraltar carrying suspected Iranian crude bound for Syria, prompting Iran to summon the UK ambassador and call the act an 'illegal seizure'. This followed earlier US sanctions on Iran and Saudi warnings about consequences if Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz.
mechanism: Escalating state-to-state confrontation over oil tanker traffic and the Strait of Hormuz raises geopolitical risk premia in energy markets and broader risk sentiment, as market participants price in the probability of supply disruption or military escalation between Iran and Western/Gulf powers.

claims.claim: The US announced major new sanctions against Iran early in the window to prevent it obtaining nuclear weapons.
Saudi Arabia warned of a 'very, very strong reaction' if Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz.
Saudi Arabia later said it would work with Japan and other nations on a plan to ensure safe tanker transit through the Persian Gulf and called for 'action' on Iran.
Royal Marines seized an oil tanker off Gibraltar suspected of carrying Iranian crude oil to Syria in breach of EU sanctions, leading Iran to summon the UK ambassador and call it an illegal seizure.
